findings.where: Last section, "Hostelworld, for comparison" (desktop-02, phone-02), which is also where the page ends
findings.fault: The page names a competitor and sets its scoring against Manta's, ending on the line that a hostel 'can look thin there'. The brief says Manta's public claim names no competitor, and it holds even its own direct-booking claim off the site while the Hostelworld application is pending. Because this section comes last, a trust page ends on a rival's method, not on Manta's promise.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the positioning names no competitor and Hostelworld's consent is still pending. A backpacker may also object: a page meant to build trust that closes by criticising another site reads as a sales pitch, not a published method.

findings.where: First screen: the lead paragraph, the summary sentence and the three-item list under "How we rank", then the first sentence of "Ranking method"
findings.fault: The first screen says the same thing three times. The lead paragraph talks about the page itself. A summary sentence then states the recency and area-average rules. A list states them again, and 'No hostel can pay for a higher position' appears a fourth time as the first line of the next section. The page's one promise is set as list item 1 in body type, so it never stands out over the text that repeats it.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker checking on a phone whether the ranking can be bought. They must read through repeated text to find that promise, and nothing marks it as the answer.

findings.where: "Ranking method" section (four long paragraphs), and the single long sentence in the Hostelworld section
findings.fault: The section is an unbroken block of long, rule-heavy sentences at one weight. Nothing in it stands out, such as a lead line per rule or a key number. The concrete mechanics are hidden in the text: no default sort by review count, 'No reviews yet' only at zero, and stay month as the guest's own claim. On a phone, this section runs past two screens of grey text.
findings.who_objects: The primary visitor, a backpacker skimming mid-trip on a phone. They will give up before reaching the rules that would earn their trust.

findings.fault: The page reads as a plain policy document: one text column on sand, with no illustration, mascot or bold claim anywhere. The brand names sterile and corporate as its enemy and asks for a loud claim with calm mechanics beneath it. This page has only the calm half.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brand's north star is 'loud moments, calm machine' and here the brand is barely visible beyond the nav bar. A first-time visitor may also find it out of character with the beachy brand they arrived from.

findings.where: End of the page, after "Hostelworld, for comparison", before the footer
findings.fault: Once the reader is convinced, the page offers no next step. There is no action toward finding a hostel, and the only onward route is back up in the nav.
findings.who_objects: A traveller who came here to decide whether to trust Manta's list. Having decided, they get no prompt to go and use it.

findings.where: Top of the page, under the "How we rank" heading
findings.fault: The method has no date or version, so nothing shows when it was last changed. The page dates its Hostelworld source but not its own rules.
findings.who_objects: A careful visitor or a hostel owner checking whether the published method is current. Without a date, a published method cannot be held to account.

findings.where: The three-item summary list under the intro, and the 100% / 50% / 25% list in "Scoring method"
findings.fault: Both lists are numbered, which suggests steps or a ranking. The first holds three separate principles, and the second holds three points on one decay curve.
findings.who_objects: A reader who takes the numbers to mean an order of priority or a sequence of steps that doesn't exist.

findings.where: Desktop: the left-aligned text column against the centred footer
findings.fault: The content is a narrow column pinned to the left, under the left-aligned wordmark, with about two-thirds of the screen empty to its right. The footer then switches to centred, so the page's line of alignment breaks at the end.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor, who sees a lopsided page that looks unfinished. Few would notice it beyond that impression.
